{{% callout type="info" %}}
**Where to find it:** Applications & Components → Comma → Model Edit → `uSwap` (also on the Comma ribbon tab, Model Edit group)
{{% /callout %}}

Reverses the direction (the handles) of selected objects. It does not exchange the locations of two objects.

**How to use:**

1.  Choose which families to include in the dialog (a selection limit of 0 means unlimited) and click **Apply**. Preselected objects are used once; after that you pick interactively.
2.  Finish each selection to reverse its handles. <kbd>Esc</kbd> ends the command.

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Families** | Beams, Polybeams, Plates, Bolts, Construction objects, Reinforcement and Items. |
| **Selection limit** | Largest number of objects per run; 0 = unlimited. |

Swap only reverses the handles and never changes the profile. A symmetric profile keeps its exact solid; an asymmetric profile (for example an HZ sheet pile) is reversed anyway, but its solid is then not the mirror of the original, and a warning appears under the prompt line with the object ID and profile — check those objects.

Reinforcement: planar SingleRebar and open polygonal RebarGroup are reversed with their hooks, bend-radius order, group end covers and distribution. Item (Brep) parts are reversed like beams. Bolt arrays, RebarSet, mesh and strand targets are skipped and listed even when their family is ticked.

The whole selection is prepared and checked before any write. Objects Swap cannot reverse (unsupported types, non-BEAM native subtypes, deformed parts, component-owned objects) are left unchanged and listed after the run. Select hosts and their reinforcement or bolts in separate runs.

{{% callout type="warning" %}}
After a native failure partial changes can remain: inspect the reported object and use Undo.
{{% /callout %}}

**More details:**

-   The whole enabled selection is prepared and checked before any writes.
-   An object Swap cannot reverse (no writer for its type yet, or a refused safety gate) is left unchanged and listed after the run; every other object is reversed.
-   Select hosts and their reinforcement or bolts in separate runs; related targets in one selection are rejected before writes.
-   Beam offset/Position compensation and catalog reflection checks protect physical placement.
-   An asymmetric profile (for example HZ sheet piles) is reversed anyway, but its solid is then not the mirror of the original: a warning appears under the prompt line with the object ID and profile, so check those objects.
-   All recorded phase, typed UDAs, attachment and assembly checks must remain valid.
-   Directionally ambiguous source chains or groups are rejected before any write.
-   For rebar groups, *Rebar groups: bar shape* reverses the bars of each group and *Rebar groups: range* reverses the pick line of a normal group (its first bar becomes its last); switch on either or both.
-   Range changes nothing else, so an uneven spacing, exclusion or cover is mirrored, exactly as if the range had been picked the other way round.
-   Tapered, spiral, tapered-curved and circle groups are skipped for range and listed after the run.
-   Item (Brep) parts are reversed like beams: start and end points swap, Position and point offsets are compensated, and the profile is kept; if the item's shape is not verified symmetric a warning is shown.
-   Bolt arrays, RebarSet, Mesh and Strand targets are skipped and listed until their writers are added, even when their family checkbox is enabled.
